question_text: Write a letter to your friend about the sight you saw and your impression of it.
answer_text:

question_text: "The hand that mocked them, and the heart that fed." Whose hand and heart has the poet referred to in this line?
answer_text: The hand is the sculptor's hand who made the statue and the heart of the King Ozymandias which fed on the passions of his people.
difficulty_reasoning: Direct recall of the poem's content.

subject: english_literature
question_text: "My name is Ozymandias, king of kings:" Why does Ozymandias refer to himself as King of Kings? What quality of the king is revealed through this statement?
answer_text: Ozymandias is the mighty king who has defeated almost all the kings and their empires around him. He is proud of his glory and power. So, he calls himself ‘King of Kings’. This statement shows that the king must be very proud of his achievements. He is a real snob.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of the character and context.

subject: english_literature
question_text: "Look on my works, ye Mighty, and despair!" Who is Ozymandias referring to when he speaks of ye Mighty? Why should they despair?
answer_text: Ozymandias refers to all the other rulers to come after his reign. They should despair, because according to him, they can’t surpass his glory and power.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires interpretation of the poem's message.

subject: english_literature
question_text: Bring out the irony in the poem.
answer_text: Ozymandias was very powerful ruler. No ruler in that time withstand against him. He was all high and mighty king. But now, his statue is present in broken pieces and has mixed with the dust and sand. Here is irony.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding of the poem's themes and deeper meanings.

subject: english_literature
question_text: 'Nothing beside remains.' What does the narrator mean when he says these words?
answer_text: When the narrator says these words, he emphasises on the fact that human life is time bound. The power and popularity of the ruler descended with the descent of the ruler. Nothing is immortal and immutable in this world.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires comprehension of the poem's message about mortality.

subject: english_literature
question_text: What is your impression of Ozymandias as a king?
answer_text: Ozymandias was a great powerful king as he had defeated almost every king in his empire. His achievements could be seen throughout the empire. But his boastful nature, his arrogance, and his nature of showing others down make him a weak person.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves personal interpretation and analysis of character.

subject: english_literature
question_text: What message is conveyed through this poem?
answer_text: Through this poem a very important message is conveyed that time is all powerful. No king or his power can defeat time. All the achievement, in the end, leads to grave as nothing lives in the world forever. So, the pride and the showcase of power are useless. The greatness of a man is known by his good deeds.
final_answer: Thus, the poem conveys that time ultimately overcomes all power and pride.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding the themes and messages of the poem.

subject: english_literature
question_text: Imagine that Ozymandias comes back to life and as he sees the condition of his statue, realisation dawns on him and he pens his thoughts in a diary. As Ozymandias, make this diary entry in about 150 words. You could begin like this: I thought I was the mightiest of all but...
answer_text:
Dear Diary,
I thought I was the mightiest of all but now I see the ruins of my once-great statue, a mere shadow of my former glory. The sands of time have eroded not just my image but the very essence of my power. I commanded respect and fear, yet here I lie, forgotten and broken. My words, carved in stone, now echo in the emptiness of the desert. I realize that no matter how great a king I was, time is the true ruler. My legacy is but a fleeting memory, a reminder that all power fades. I wish I had focused on kindness and wisdom rather than pride and tyranny. Perhaps then, I would have been remembered not for my might, but for my deeds. Time has taught me that true greatness lies in humility and compassion.
final_answer: Thus, I understand that my might was temporary, but my actions could have left a lasting impact.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires creative thinking and understanding of the poem's themes.

subject: english_literature
question_text: 'Ozymandias' and 'Not Marble, nor the Gilded Monuments' are on Time. Compare the two sonnets in terms of the way in which Time is treated by the poets. Write your answer in about 150 words.
answer_text: In both the sonnets, ‘Ozymandias’ and ‘Not Marble Not the Gilded Monuments’ time is presented in different way by the poets. In ‘Ozymandias’, S.T. Coleridge presents time more powerful than the most of the powerful king. On the other hand, in ‘Not Marble Not the Gilded Monuments’, Shakespeare present time as powerful but not as powerful and long lasting as his words for his friends. In ‘Ozymandias’ it is seen that even a great king is forgotten in the course of time if his deeds are bad. But if you love someone more than anything else in the world, as mention in ‘Not Marble Not the Gilded Monuments’, your love for that person lives forever. In such case, one doesn’t need to make a statue to make the memory live forever. Time can be won only by love not by hate.
final_answer: Thus, the treatment of time in both sonnets highlights the transient nature of power and the enduring quality of love.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of themes in poetry and comparative analysis.
